questions: How is Match Betting settled in cricket?
What happens if a cricket match has no official result?
How is a tie settled in Match Betting?
What happens if a match is cancelled?
How long after the advertised start time must a cancelled match be restarted?
content: Match Betting is settled on who wins the match according to official competition rules. Results affected by weather are settled on the official result, and bets are void if there is no official result. A tie is settled by dead heat rules unless the competition rules determine a winner via bowl-off, super over or similar, in which case the official result stands. In First Class Matches a tie is settled as a dead-heat between both teams, with draw bets losing. If a match is discontinued due to external factors, bets are void unless a winner is declared under the competition rules. If a cancelled match is not replayed or restarted within 36 hours of its advertised start time, all bets are void.

questions: How is Double Chance settled in cricket?
What happens to Double Chance bets in a tie?
Are Double Chance bets void if there is no official result?
content: Double Chance covers whether the match result will be one of two of the three possible outcomes. A tie is settled as a dead heat, and all bets are settled according to official competition rules. If there is no official result, all bets are void.

questions: How does Draw No Bet work in cricket?
What happens to Draw No Bet wagers if the match is drawn?
How is a tie settled under Draw No Bet?
content: Draw No Bet settles on the match winner, with all bets voided if the match ends in a draw. A tie is settled as a dead heat, and settlement otherwise follows official competition rules, with bets void if there is no official result.

questions: How is the Toss Winner market settled?
What happens if no toss takes place?
Does a bat flip count as a toss?
content: Toss Winner settles on which team wins the coin toss. If no toss takes place, all bets are void. Equivalents to a coin toss, such as a bat flip, are treated as a toss for settlement purposes.

questions: What is the Toss/Win Double market?
How is Toss/Win Double settled?
content: Toss/Win Double requires correctly predicting both the toss winner and the match winner. It is settled according to the same rules as Toss Winner and Match Betting respectively.

questions: How is the Tied Match market settled?
What counts as a tie in First Class matches?
What happens if the match is abandoned?
content: Tied Match bets are settled according to the official result, and are void if the match is abandoned or there is no official result. In First Class matches, a tie occurs when the side batting second is bowled out for a second time with the scores level.

questions: How is Most Fours settled?
Do overthrows count towards fours?
What overs threshold applies for Most Fours in a drawn First Class match?
Do fours in a super over count?
content: Most Fours settles on which team hits the most fours. Bets are void in limited overs matches if at least 80% of the scheduled overs in either innings are not completed due to external factors, unless settlement was already determined. In drawn First Class matches, bets are void if fewer than 200 overs are bowled, unless already determined. Only fours from the bat, whether off legal or illegal deliveries, count; overthrows, all-run fours, extras and super over fours do not count. In First Class games, only first innings fours count.

questions: How is Most Sixes settled?
Do sixes in a super over count?
What is the overs threshold for a drawn First Class match?
content: Most Sixes settles on which team hits the most sixes, using the same voiding conditions as Most Fours. Only sixes struck from the bat, off legal or illegal deliveries, count; overthrows, extras and super over sixes do not count. In First Class games, only first innings sixes count.

questions: How is Most Extras settled?
What counts as an extra?
Do extras in a super over count?
content: Most Extras settles on which team has the most extras added to their batting score, subject to the same voiding thresholds as Most Fours. Wide deliveries, no balls, byes, leg byes and penalty runs all count. If a delivery produces both runs off the bat and extras, only the extras count toward this market. Extras in a super over do not count, and in First Class games only first innings extras count.

questions: How is Most Run Outs Conceded settled?
What does 'conceded' mean for this market?
Do run outs in a super over count?
content: Most Run Outs Conceded settles on which team concedes more run outs, meaning members of that team are run out while batting. Voiding thresholds follow the same rules as Most Fours. Run outs in a super over do not count, and in First Class games only first innings run outs count.

questions: How is Highest First Over settled?
What happens if the first over is not completed?
Do extras count in the first over market?
content: Highest First Over settles on which team scores more runs in the first over of their innings. The first over must be completed for bets to stand, unless settlement is already determined. If the innings ends during the first over due to external factors, bets are void, unless already determined. In First Class matches this applies only to each team's first innings, and extras and penalty runs in that over count towards settlement.

section.title: Most Runs in Groups of Overs

questions: How is Most Runs in Groups of Overs settled?
What happens if the specified overs are not completed?
Does a declaration affect settlement?
content: Most Runs in Groups of Overs settles on which team scores more runs after a specified number of overs of their innings. Bets are void if the specified overs are not completed, unless the team is all out, declares, reaches its target, or settlement is already determined. In limited overs matches, bets are void if less than 80% of the specified overs are bowled due to external factors, unless already determined. In First Class matches this applies only to each team's first innings.

questions: How is Highest First Partnership settled?
What happens if no wicket falls before the innings ends?
Does a batsman retiring hurt count as a wicket for this market?
content: Highest First Partnership settles on which team scores more runs before losing their first wicket. If the batting team reaches the end of their overs, their target, or declares before losing a wicket, the result is the total runs scored. A batsman retiring hurt does not count as a wicket. Bets are void in limited overs matches if the innings is reduced due to external factors, unless already determined, and in drawn First Class matches if fewer than 200 overs are bowled. In First Class matches, this applies only to each team's first innings.

questions: How is Match Fours settled?
Do overthrows count towards Match Fours?
What is the void threshold for Match Fours?
content: Match Fours settles on the total number of fours hit in the match. Voiding thresholds are the same as Most Fours. Only fours from the bat, off legal or illegal deliveries, count; overthrows, all-run fours, extras and super over fours do not count.

questions: How is Match Sixes settled?
Do sixes in a super over count towards Match Sixes?
What is the void threshold for Match Sixes?
content: Match Sixes settles on the total number of sixes hit in the match, using the same voiding thresholds as Most Fours. Only sixes from the bat, off legal or illegal deliveries, count; overthrows, extras and super over sixes do not count.

questions: How is Match Extras settled?
What deliveries count as extras for this market?
Do extras in a super over count?
content: Match Extras settles on the total extras scored in the match, using the same voiding thresholds as Most Fours. Wide deliveries, no balls, byes, leg byes and penalty runs count; if runs off the bat and extras both occur off the same delivery, only the extras count. Extras in a super over do not count.

questions: How is Match Wides settled?
Do penalty runs count towards Match Wides?
Do wides in a super over count?
content: Match Wides settles on the total wides scored in the match, using the same voiding thresholds as Most Fours. Any runs resulting from a wide delivery, except penalty runs, count towards the total. Wides in a super over do not count.

questions: How is Match Run Outs settled?
Do run outs in a super over count?
content: Match Run Outs settles on the total run outs in the match, using the same voiding thresholds as Most Fours. Run outs occurring in a super over do not count.

questions: How is Match Wickets settled?
Does retiring hurt count as a wicket?
Do wickets in a super over count?
content: Match Wickets settles on the total wickets falling in the match, using the same voiding thresholds as Most Fours. Retired hurt does not count as a dismissal, and wickets taken in a super over do not count.

questions: How is Match Ducks settled?
What counts as a duck?
Do ducks in a super over count?
content: Match Ducks settles on the total ducks scored in the match, using the same voiding thresholds as Most Fours. A duck is a dismissal for zero runs; retired hurt does not count as a dismissal, and ducks in a super over do not count.

questions: How is Match Milestones settled?
Does a century count as both a fifty and a hundred?
What voids Match Milestones bets?
content: Match Milestones settles on how many individual innings of 50+ or 100+ runs are scored in the match. A score over 100 counts as both a fifty and a hundred. In limited overs matches, bets are void if less than 80% of the scheduled overs are completed due to external factors, unless already determined.

questions: How is Maximum Over in Match settled?
Do extras count towards the maximum over?
How does this market apply to The Hundred?
content: Maximum Over in Match settles on the highest number of runs scored in a single over of the match, using the same voiding thresholds as Most Fours. All runs, including extras, count; super overs do not count. For The Hundred, an over consists of 5 legal deliveries, making a full innings 20 overs, with all other rules unchanged.

questions: How is Match Top Batter settled?
What happens if a named batter is replaced by a concussion substitute?
What if a batter does not bat?
How are ties settled in Match Top Batter?
content: Match Top Batter settles on the batter with the highest individual score in the match. Bets are void in limited overs matches if less than 50% of the scheduled overs in either innings are completed at the time the bet was placed due to external factors. For First Class matches this applies only to each team's first innings, and is void if fewer than 200 overs are bowled, unless already determined. A player named at the toss who is later replaced by a concussion substitute still counts, as does the replacement. A named batter who does not bat still has bets stand. If a batter is substituted after the in-play market is offered, the original market is settled as normal and a new market may be offered. Ties are settled by dead heat rules, and runs scored in a super over do not count.

questions: How is Match Top Bowler settled?
How are ties broken in Match Top Bowler?
What happens if no bowler takes a wicket?
What if an unnamed substitute takes the most wickets?
content: Match Top Bowler settles on the bowler with the most wickets in the match. Voiding thresholds follow Match Top Batter. A player named at the toss but replaced by a concussion sub still counts, as does the replacement. A named bowler who does not bowl still has bets stand, but if an unnamed substitute takes the most wickets, bets are void. Ties are broken first by fewest runs conceded, then dead heat rules apply if still level. Wickets in a super over do not count, and if no bowler takes a wicket in an innings, all bets are void.

questions: How is Team of Top Batter settled?
What if both teams' top batters score the same?
What happens if a match is curtailed after settlement is determined?
content: Team of Top Batter settles on which team contains the match's top batter, following the same rules as Match Top Batter, with dead heat rules applying if the top batters from both teams score equally. If settlement was already determined before the match was curtailed, bets stand.

questions: How is Team of Top Bowler settled?
What if both teams' top bowlers take the same number of wickets?
content: Team of Top Bowler settles on which team contains the match's top bowler, following the same rules as Match Top Bowler, with dead heat rules applying if the top bowlers from both teams take equal wickets. If settlement was already determined before the match was curtailed, bets stand.

questions: How is Player of the Match settled?
What happens if no player of the match is declared?
Are substitutes eligible for Player of the Match?
content: Player of the Match settles on the officially declared player of the match, with dead heat rules applying to shared awards. If no player of the match is officially declared, all bets are void. All players who played, including substitutes, are eligible for settlement, and bets on a player who did not play are void.

questions: How is First Innings Lead settled?
What happens if the first innings runs are equal?
What overs threshold applies to a drawn First Class match?
content: First Innings Lead settles on the run deficit between first innings in a First Class match. Both first innings must be completed, and dead heat rules apply in the case of a tie. In drawn First Class matches, bets are void if fewer than 200 overs are bowled, unless settlement is already determined.

questions: How is Fifty/Hundred in Match settled?
What score counts as a fifty or a hundred?
content: Fifty/Hundred in Match settles on whether any batter scores 50 or more, or 100 or more, in the match. Voiding thresholds follow the same rules as Most Fours.

questions: How is Fifty/Hundred in First Innings settled?
Does this market apply to both teams' first innings in First Class cricket?
content: Fifty/Hundred in First Innings settles on whether any batter scores 50 or more, or 100 or more, in the first innings of the match. In limited overs matches, bets are void if less than 80% of the first innings overs are completed due to external factors, unless already determined. In drawn First Class matches, the innings must be completed or exceed 200 overs, unless already determined. This market refers only to the first innings of the match overall, not both teams' first innings.

questions: How is Highest Individual Score settled?
How are ties handled in Highest Individual Score?
content: Highest Individual Score settles on the highest score by a batter in the match, using the same voiding thresholds as Most Fours, with dead heat rules applying to ties.

questions: How is Runs off Delivery settled?
How are illegal deliveries numbered for settlement?
Do free hit re-bowled deliveries count?
How does this market apply to The Hundred?
content: Runs off Delivery settles on the runs added to the team total off a specified delivery. All illegal balls count as deliveries for numbering purposes, so a wide as the first ball of an over is settled as delivery 1, and the next ball as delivery 2. Runs scored off an additional free hit delivery, or a re-bowled illegal delivery, do not count. All runs, whether off the bat or not, are included; for example a wide with three extra runs counts as 4 runs off that delivery. For The Hundred, an over consists of 5 legal deliveries, so a full innings is 20 overs, and deliveries are numbered accordingly.

questions: How is Runs in Over settled?
What happens if the specified over is not completed?
Do penalty runs count towards Runs in Over?
content: Runs in Over settles on the runs scored in a specified over, which must be completed for bets to stand unless settlement is already determined. If the innings ends during the over it is deemed complete, unless ended due to external factors, in which case bets are void unless already determined. If the over never commences, bets are void. Extras and penalty runs count, unless penalty runs end the innings or match before a ball is bowled in the over, in which case the over is void. If a run out ends the game during the bowler's run up with no deliveries completed, bets are void. For The Hundred, an over consists of 5 legal deliveries.

questions: How is Boundary in Over settled?
What counts as a boundary for this market?
content: Boundary in Over settles on whether a boundary is scored in a specified over, following the same rules as Runs in Over. Only boundaries from the bat, off legal or illegal deliveries, count; overthrows, all-run fours and extras do not count.

questions: How is Wicket in Over settled?
Do run outs count as wickets for this market?
What happens if a batsman is timed out during the over?
content: Wicket in Over settles on whether a wicket falls in a specified over, following the same rules as Runs in Over. Any wicket, including run outs, counts. A batsman retiring hurt does not count as a wicket, but if a batsman is timed out or retired out, the wicket is deemed to have occurred on the previous ball.

questions: How is Over Odd/Even settled?
Is zero considered odd or even?
content: Over Odd/Even settles on whether the runs scored in a specified over are odd or even, following the same rules as Runs in Over. Zero is deemed to be an even number.

questions: How is Runs in Groups of Overs settled?
What happens if the specified overs are not completed?
How does this market apply to The Hundred?
content: Runs in Groups of Overs settles on the runs scored across a specified number of overs. Bets are void if the overs are not completed, unless the team is all out, declares, reaches its target or settlement is already determined. Extras and penalty runs in that group of overs count. In limited overs matches, bets are void if the innings is reduced at any stage to less than 80% of the stated maximum overs at the time the bet was placed, unless already determined. For The Hundred, an over consists of 5 legal deliveries.

questions: How is Wickets in Groups of Overs settled?
What happens if a batter is timed out during the group of overs?
How does this market apply to The Hundred?
content: Wickets in Groups of Overs settles on the wickets falling across a specified number of overs, using the same voiding conditions as Runs in Groups of Overs. If a batter is timed out or retired out, the wicket is deemed to have occurred on the previous ball; retired hurt does not count as a dismissal. For The Hundred, an over consists of 5 legal deliveries.

questions: How is Runs in Session settled?
What happens if fewer than 20 overs are bowled in the session?
content: Runs in Session settles on the total runs scored in a specified session, regardless of which team scores them. If fewer than 20 overs are bowled in the session, bets are void unless settlement is already determined.

questions: How is Innings Runs settled?
What happens if a team declares?
What overs thresholds apply to drawn First Class matches?
content: Innings Runs settles on the runs a team scores in a specified innings. In limited overs matches, bets are void if less than 80% of the scheduled overs are completed at the time the bet was placed due to external factors, unless already determined. Bets on a future innings remain valid regardless of runs scored in earlier innings. In drawn First Class matches, bets are void if fewer than 200 overs are bowled, and also void if an incomplete innings has fewer than 60 overs bowled, unless already determined. A declaration is treated as completing the innings.

questions: How is Innings Wickets settled?
Does retiring hurt count as a wicket for this market?
What happens if the team declares?
content: Innings Wickets settles on the wickets lost by the batting team in the current innings. Voiding thresholds follow Innings Runs. Retired hurt does not count as a dismissal, and a declaration is treated as completing the innings.

questions: How is Innings Fours settled?
content: Innings Fours settles on the fours hit by the batting team in their current innings, following the same rules as Most Fours.

questions: How is Innings Sixes settled?
content: Innings Sixes settles on the sixes hit by the batting team in their current innings, following the same rules as Most Sixes.

questions: How is Innings Extras settled?
content: Innings Extras settles on the extras added to the named team's innings, following the same rules as Most Extras.

questions: How is Innings Wides Conceded settled?
content: Innings Wides Conceded settles on the wides bowled by the named bowling team in the innings, following the same rules as Match Wides.

questions: How is Innings Ducks settled?
content: Innings Ducks settles on the ducks scored in the named team's batting innings, following the same rules as Match Ducks.

questions: How is Innings Run Outs settled?
content: Innings Run Outs settles on the run outs conceded in the innings, following the same rules as Most Extras.

questions: How is Maximum Over in Innings settled?
content: Maximum Over in Innings settles on the highest scoring over in the current innings, following the same rules as Maximum Over in Match.

questions: How is Innings Runs Odd or Even settled?
What voids this market?
content: Innings Runs, Odd or Even settles on whether the total innings runs are odd or even. If the innings is abandoned, forfeited, or there is no official result, all bets are void.

section.title: Innings to finish with a Boundary

questions: How is Innings to Finish with a Boundary settled?
What happens if overs are reduced before the bet was placed?
content: Innings to Finish with a Boundary settles on whether the last ball of the innings is a boundary. Only boundaries from the bat, off legal or illegal deliveries, count; overthrows, all-run fours and extras do not count. In limited overs matches, bets are void if there is any reduction in the scheduled overs after the bet was placed due to external factors. If the match is abandoned or there is no official result, all bets are void.

questions: How is Top Batter in Innings settled?
What happens if a substitute batter scores the most runs?
How are ties settled?
content: Top Batter in Innings settles on the batter with the highest individual score for the named team's innings. Bets are void in limited overs matches if less than 50% of the scheduled overs are completed at the time of the bet due to external factors. Pre-match bets for First Class matches apply only to each team's first innings, and are void if fewer than 200 overs are bowled, unless already determined. A player replaced by a concussion sub still counts, as does the replacement. If a batter is substituted in after the in-play market is offered, the original market is settled as normal and a new market may be offered. Dead heat rules apply to ties, and runs scored in a super over do not count.

questions: How is Top Bowler in Innings settled?
How are ties broken?
What happens if no bowler takes a wicket in the innings?
content: Top Bowler in Innings settles on the bowler with the most wickets in the named team's innings, using the same voiding thresholds and substitute rules as Top Batter in Innings. Ties are broken first by fewest runs conceded, then by dead heat rules. Wickets in a super over do not count, and if no bowler takes a wicket, all bets are void.

questions: How is Last Player Standing settled?
What happens if two batters are both not out at the end?
What happens if more than 11 players bat?
content: Last Player Standing settles on which batter is not out when the innings ends. If two or more batters are not out, the winner is the last one to face a delivery, legal or not. A player who retired hurt and did not return to the crease is not deemed not out. If more than 11 players bat, the market is void. In limited overs matches, bets are void if the innings is subsequently reduced due to external factors after the bet was placed. All players, including substitutes, are eligible for settlement.

questions: How is Most Economical Bowler settled?
Do wides and no-balls count towards runs conceded?
How are ties settled?
content: Most Economical Bowler settles on the bowler with the lowest runs conceded per over in an innings. To match the scorecard, wides and no-balls count towards runs conceded, but byes, leg byes and penalty runs do not. A bowler named in the starting XI who does not bowl still has bets stand. Pre-match bets for First Class matches apply only to each team's first innings, and are void if fewer than 200 overs are bowled, unless already determined. A player replaced by a concussion sub still counts, as does the replacement. Ties are settled by dead heat rules, and runs conceded in a super over do not count.

questions: How is Batter Runs settled?
What happens if the batter is not out at the end of the innings?
What happens if the batter does not bat?
What happens if the batter retires hurt and does not return?
content: Batter Runs settles on how many runs the named batter scores. If the batter finishes not out, that score is the final result. If the batter does not bat, the bet is void. If a batter retires hurt but returns, their total runs in the innings count; if they do not return, the result stands at the score when they retired. In limited overs matches, bets are void if less than 80% of the scheduled overs are completed due to external factors, unless settlement is already, or goes on to be, determined — determined meaning the specified line is passed or the batter is dismissed. In drawn First Class matches, bets are void if fewer than 200 overs are bowled. For pre-match bets, only the batter's first innings counts, and runs in a super over do not count.

questions: How is Combined Batsman Runs settled?
What happens if one of the named batters does not bat?
content: Combined Batsman Runs settles on the total runs scored by the named batters combined, following the same rules as Batter Runs. If any named batter does not bat, the bet is void, unless settlement is already, or goes on to be, determined.

questions: How is Batter Fours settled?
What happens if the batter retires hurt?
content: Batter Fours settles on how many fours the named batter hits, following the same not-out, retired hurt and voiding rules as Batter Runs. Only fours from the bat, off legal or illegal deliveries, count; overthrows, all-run fours and extras do not count. For pre-match bets, only the batter's first innings counts, and fours in a super over do not count.

questions: How is Batter Sixes settled?
What happens if the batter retires hurt?
content: Batter Sixes settles on how many sixes the named batter hits, following the same not-out, retired hurt and voiding rules as Batter Runs. Only sixes from the bat, off legal or illegal deliveries, count; overthrows and extras do not count. For pre-match bets, only the batter's first innings counts, and sixes in a super over do not count.

questions: How is Batter Milestones settled?
content: Batter Milestones settles on whether the named batter reaches a specified run milestone, following the same rules as Batter Runs.

questions: How is Batter Deliveries Faced settled?
Do wides count as deliveries faced?
Do no-balls count as deliveries faced?
content: Batter Deliveries Faced settles on how many deliveries the named batter faces. To match the scorecard, wides do not count but no-balls do. If the batter retires hurt but returns, deliveries faced across the innings count; if they do not return, the result stands at the point they retired. Voiding rules follow Batter Runs. For pre-match bets, only the batter's first innings counts, and deliveries faced in a super over do not count.

questions: How is Batter Method of Dismissal settled?
What happens if the batter is not out?
Is caught and bowled included as a catch?
content: Batter Method of Dismissal settles on how the named batter is dismissed. If the batter is not out, all bets are void. If the batter retires and does not return, bets are void; if they return and are later out, bets stand. Caught and bowled dismissals are included within the fielder catch category.

questions: How is Bowler Wickets settled?
What happens if the bowler does not bowl?
content: Bowler Wickets settles on how many wickets the named bowler takes. If the bowler does not bowl, bets are void. In limited overs matches, bets are void if less than 80% of the scheduled overs in the relevant innings are completed due to external factors, unless already determined — determined meaning the specified line is passed. In drawn First Class matches, bets are void if fewer than 200 overs are bowled, unless the bowler's innings is complete. For pre-match bets, only the bowler's first innings counts, and wickets in a super over do not count.

questions: How is Bowler Runs Conceded settled?
Do wides and no-balls count as runs conceded?
content: Bowler Runs Conceded settles on how many runs the named bowler concedes. To match the scorecard, wides and no-balls count, but byes, leg byes and penalty runs do not. If the bowler does not bowl, bets are void. In limited overs matches, bets are void if less than 80% of the scheduled overs are completed due to external factors, unless settlement is already, or goes on to be, determined. In drawn First Class matches, bets are void if fewer than 200 overs are bowled. For pre-match bets, only the bowler's first innings counts, and runs conceded in a super over do not count.

questions: How is Named Player Player Performance settled?
How many points are awarded per run, wicket, catch and stumping?
What happens if the player is not in the starting eleven?
content: Named Player Player Performance settles on points scored under the performance scoring system: 1 point per run scored, 20 points per wicket taken, 10 points per catch taken, and 25 points per stumping. A player in the starting eleven who does not bat or bowl is still settled. If the player is not in the starting eleven, bets are void. In limited overs matches, bets are void if less than 80% of the scheduled overs are completed due to external factors, unless settlement is already determined. In drawn First Class matches, bets are void if fewer than 200 overs are bowled, unless both first innings are completed. In First Class games, only first innings points count, and points in a super over do not count.

questions: How is Batter Matchbet settled?
What happens if a named player does not bat?
content: Batter Matchbet settles on which of two named players scores the most runs. In limited overs matches, bets are void if less than 80% of the scheduled overs are completed due to external factors. In drawn First Class matches, bets are void if fewer than 200 overs are bowled, unless already determined. Both players must be named in the starting XI or appear as a substitute; if either does not then bat, bets are still settled. Runs in a super over do not count.

questions: How is Bowler Matchbet settled?
What happens if a named player does not bowl?
content: Bowler Matchbet settles on which of two named players takes the most wickets, using the same voiding thresholds as Batter Matchbet. Both players must be named in the starting XI or appear as a substitute; if either does not then bowl, bets are still settled. Wickets in a super over do not count.

questions: How is All-Rounder Matchbet settled?
How are points scored for this market?
content: All-Rounder Matchbet settles on which of two named players scores the most points under the performance scoring system: 1 point per run, 20 per wicket, 10 per catch, 25 per stumping. Voiding thresholds follow Batter Matchbet. Both players must be named in the starting XI or appear as a substitute; if either does not then bat or bowl, bets are still settled. Points in a super over do not count.

questions: How is Keeper Matchbet settled?
What if a keeper's role changes during the match?
content: Keeper Matchbet settles on which of two named wicket keepers scores more points under the same performance scoring system as All-Rounder Matchbet. Voiding thresholds follow Batter Matchbet. Both players must start the match as wicket keeper, or appear as a substitute keeper, but bets are settled according to the scoring system even if their playing role later changes. Points in a super over do not count.

questions: How is Fall of Next Wicket settled?
What happens if the innings ends before the next wicket falls?
content: Fall of Next Wicket settles on the team score when the next wicket falls. If the partnership ends at the end of the innings, bets settle at the final score. Retiring hurt does not count as a wicket. In limited overs matches, bets are void if less than 80% of the scheduled overs are completed due to external factors, unless settlement is already, or goes on to be, determined — determined meaning the specified line is passed or the wicket falls. In drawn First Class matches, bets are void if fewer than 200 overs are bowled.

questions: How is Next Player Out settled?
What happens if the named batters change before the wicket falls?
content: Next Player Out settles on which batter is next to be dismissed. If either named batter retires hurt, or the batters at the crease differ from those quoted, both bets are void. If no more wickets fall, all bets are void.

questions: How is Method of Next Wicket Dismissal settled?
Does retiring hurt count as the next wicket?
What happens if the specified wicket does not fall?
content: Method of Next Wicket Dismissal settles on how the next wicket falls. Retiring hurt does not count as a wicket. If a batter is retired out, all bets are void. If the specified wicket does not fall, all bets are void. Caught and bowled dismissals are included within the fielder catch category.

questions: How is Race to 'X' Runs settled?
What happens if neither batter reaches the target runs?
content: Race to 'X' Runs settles on which named batter reaches a specified run total first. All bets stand regardless of any curtailment. If neither batter reaches the specified total, the market settles as 'Neither'.

questions: How is Next Boundary Four or Six settled?
What happens if there are no more boundaries in the innings?
content: Next Boundary Four or Six settles on whether the next boundary scored is a four or a six. If there are no more boundaries in the innings, bets are void. Only boundaries from the bat, off legal or illegal deliveries, count; overthrows, all-run fours and extras do not count. In limited overs matches, bets are void if the innings is reduced at any stage to less than 80% of the stated maximum overs at the time the bet was placed, unless already determined. In drawn First Class matches, bets are void if fewer than 200 overs are bowled. Boundaries in a super over do not count.

questions: How is Winning Over settled?
What happens if there is no official result?
content: Winning Over settles on which over of the named team's innings the match is completed in. All bets are void if there is no official result. In limited overs matches, all bets are void if the maximum overs possible are subsequently reduced in any way after the bet was placed.

questions: How is Both Teams to Score 'X' Runs settled?
Which innings count for this market?
What overs threshold applies to drawn First Class matches?
content: Both Teams to Score 'X' Runs settles on whether both teams score a specified number of runs. Each innings is judged complete if at least 80% of the scheduled overs at the time the bet was placed have been bowled, in line with Innings Runs rules. In drawn First Class matches, bets are void if fewer than 100 overs are bowled in either team's first innings, unless already determined. Only runs scored in the first innings count, and a declaration is treated as completing the innings.

questions: How is Either Batter Method of Dismissal settled?
What happens if a named batter is not out at the end?
content: Either Batter Method of Dismissal settles on whether either of two named batters is dismissed by the specified method. All bets settle regardless of whether either batter remains not out or retired hurt at the end of the innings.

questions: How is Both Batters Method of Dismissal settled?
content: Both Batters Method of Dismissal settles on whether both of two named batters are dismissed by the specified method, following the same rules as Either Batter Method of Dismissal.

questions: How is Runs off Consecutive Deliveries settled?
content: Runs off Consecutive Deliveries settles the same way as Runs off Delivery, except the specified number of runs must be scored off both of the named deliveries for the bet to win.

questions: How is Wicket off Delivery settled?
Does a run out count for this market?
content: Wicket off Delivery settles on whether a wicket falls off a specified delivery, which must be completed for bets to stand. Any wicket, including run outs, counts. A batter retiring hurt does not count as a wicket, but a batter timed out or retired out is deemed dismissed on the previous ball.

section.title: Both Batters to Score 'X' Runs in Over

questions: How is Both Batters to Score 'X' Runs in Over settled?
What happens if a named batter is dismissed before the over commences?
content: Both Batters to Score 'X' Runs in Over settles on whether both named batters score the specified runs in the over, which must be completed for bets to stand unless settlement is already determined. If the innings ends during the over it is deemed complete, unless due to external factors, in which case bets are void unless already determined. If the over never commences, bets are void. Only runs off the bat count. Bets settle regardless of whether either named batter is dismissed or retires hurt before the over commences.

section.title: Both Batters to Score a Boundary in Over

questions: How is Both Batters to Score a Boundary in Over settled?
content: Both Batters to Score a Boundary in Over settles on whether both named batters hit a boundary in the over, following the same rules as Both Batters to Score 'X' Runs in Over. Both fours and sixes count as boundaries, but only if scored from the bat off legal or illegal deliveries; overthrows and all-run fours do not count.

section.title: Both a Four and a Six to be Scored in an Over

questions: How is Both a Four and a Six to be Scored in an Over settled?
content: Both a Four and a Six to be Scored in an Over settles on whether at least one four and one six are scored in the specified over, which must be completed for bets to stand unless settlement is already determined. If the innings ends during the over it is deemed complete, unless due to external factors, in which case bets are void unless already determined. If the over never commences, bets are void. Only fours and sixes from the bat, off legal or illegal deliveries, count; overthrows and all-run fours do not count.

questions: How is Batter and Bowler Combo Milestones settled?
What happens if the bowler does not bowl?
content: Batter and Bowler Combo Milestones settles on whether the named batter and named bowler both reach their specified milestones. The batter portion follows Batter Runs rules, counting only first innings runs in First Class games. For the bowler portion, a bowler who does not bowl is deemed to have taken 0 wickets. In limited overs matches, bets are void if less than 80% of the scheduled overs are completed due to external factors, unless settlement has been determined — determined meaning the specified lines are passed. In drawn First Class matches, bets are void if fewer than 200 overs are bowled, unless the bowler's innings is complete. In First Class games, only first innings runs and wickets count, and none from a super over count.

questions: How is Batters Combo Milestones settled?
content: Batters Combo Milestones settles on whether both named batters reach their specified run milestones, following the same rules as Combined Batsman Runs.

questions: How is a player sent off treated for settlement purposes?
content: A player being sent off is treated as retired out, and is therefore settled as a wicket.

questions: How are concussion or tactical substitutions treated for settlement?
Does a substitute count as playing a full part in the match?
content: A player leaving the field as a substitute does not count as a wicket. If the player does not return, the final result stands as it was when they left the field. When a player enters as a substitute, both they and the player they replaced are considered to have played a full part in the match for settlement purposes.

section.title: Penalty runs after the conclusion of an innings

questions: Do penalty runs added after an innings ends count towards that innings' markets?
content: Penalty runs added to a team's total after the other team's innings has started do not count towards settlement of markets relating to the previous innings.

questions: How are overs defined in The Hundred?
How many overs make up a full innings in The Hundred?
content: For The Hundred, an over consists of 5 legal deliveries, so a full innings is made up of 20 overs. All other rules remain the same as other limited overs formats.

questions: What happens if a match is created in the wrong format?
Is a new match created after an incorrect format error?
content: If a match is created in the wrong format, such as T20 instead of List A, all bets are void and a new match is created in the correct format.

questions: Do Aussie Rules Football bets include overtime?
Are markets settled after regular time or extra time?
How long is regular time for betting purposes?
Does injury time count in settlement?
Is extra time included in Aussie Rules betting?
What happens if a match goes into overtime?
Are bets settled after 80 minutes?
content: Unless expressly stated otherwise, all betting markets are settled based on the result at the end of the scheduled 80 minutes of regular play. Regular time includes any injury or stoppage time but does not include extra time or overtime.

questions: What happens if the match time is displayed incorrectly?
Can Aussie Rules bets be void because of an incorrect match time?
How much time difference is allowed before bets may be voided?
What if the scheduled match time is wrong?
When can the sportsbook void bets because of incorrect timing?
content: If betting odds are offered with an incorrect match time that differs by more than two minutes from the correct scheduled time, the sportsbook reserves the right to void the affected bets.

questions: What happens if the wrong teams are displayed?
Can bets be void because of incorrect team names?
What if the competition category is incorrect?
How does the sportsbook handle fixture information errors?
When are bets void due to incorrect team information?
content: If the participating teams or the competition category are displayed incorrectly, the sportsbook reserves the right to void the affected bets.

questions: What happens if a boxer fails to answer the bell?
Who wins if a fighter cannot continue into the next round?
How is the winner determined if a boxer doesn't come out for the next round?
Which round is used for settlement if a boxer retires between rounds?
content: If either fighter fails to answer the bell for the next round, the opponent is deemed to have won the contest in the previous round.

questions: What happens if a boxing match is declared a No Contest?
Are bets void if the fight ends as No Contest?
How are bets settled when a fight has no official result?
What is the betting outcome for a No Contest fight?
content: If a boxing match is officially declared a 'No Contest', all bets placed on the fight are void.

section.title: Change in Scheduled Number of Rounds

questions: What happens if the scheduled number of rounds changes?
Are Total Rounds bets void if the fight length changes?
What betting markets are void when the number of rounds is modified?
Does a change in fight length affect Method of Victory bets?
content: If the scheduled number of rounds changes before the fight begins, all Total Rounds, Round Betting, and Method of Victory markets are declared void.

questions: What is the difference between Winner and 1X2 betting?
How is a draw settled in the Winner market?
What happens if a boxing match ends in a draw?
What is a Technical Draw?
What is a Majority Draw?
Which market should I use if I want to bet on a draw?
content: The Winner market predicts which boxer wins the fight and does not include a draw option. If the fight ends in a draw, including a Majority Draw or Technical Draw, Winner bets are void. The 1X2 Fight Result market includes a Draw selection, and if the fight ends in a Majority Draw or Technical Draw, the Draw selection is settled as the winner.

questions: How are Total Rounds bets settled?
What does Over 9.5 rounds mean?
How are half rounds calculated?
What happens if a fight ends exactly at the halfway point of a round?
How does Over/Under round betting work?
content: Total Rounds (Over/Under) betting predicts the round in which the fight result will be determined. For markets with half rounds, the halfway point of the stated round (for example, 1 minute 30 seconds of Round 10 for Over/Under 9.5) is used to determine settlement. If the fight ends exactly at the halfway point, it is settled as Over.

questions: How does Winner and Exact Round betting work?
Does disqualification count as a knockout?
What happens if a boxer fails to answer the bell?
How are technical decisions settled?
What happens to round betting if there is a technical decision?
content: Winner and Exact Round betting predicts both the winning boxer and the exact round in which the fight is won by knockout (KO), technical knockout (TKO), or disqualification. If a boxer fails to answer the bell, the opponent is considered to have won in the previous round. If the fight is decided by technical decision before completion, it is settled as a decision victory and all Winner & Exact Round bets lose.

questions: How is the Winning Method market settled?
Does disqualification count as a knockout?
What methods of victory are recognized?
How are official results used for settlement?
content: Winning Method betting predicts how the fight will be won. Settlement is based on the official result. A victory by disqualification is treated as a knockout or technical knockout for settlement purposes.

questions: What does Win Inside the Distance mean?
What happens if the fight ends by technical decision?
Is a technical decision considered to have gone the distance?
How are Inside the Distance bets settled?
content: The 'Any Fighter to Win Inside the Distance' market predicts whether the fight will finish before the scheduled number of rounds. For settlement purposes, a technical decision is considered not to have gone the full distance.

questions: How are MMA bets settled?
Are MMA bets settled using the official result?
What happens if the fight result changes after the event?
Do appeals affect settled MMA bets?
Are amended results considered for settlement?
When is the official fight result determined?
content: All MMA betting markets are settled using the official fight result that is available immediately after the fight ends. Any subsequent appeals, reviews, or amendments to the official result are not considered for betting settlement.

questions: What happens if an MMA fighter fails to answer the bell?
Who wins if a fighter cannot continue into the next round?
How is the winner determined when a fighter doesn't answer the bell?
Which round is used for settlement if a fighter retires between rounds?
content: If either fighter fails to answer the bell for the next round, the opponent is deemed to have won the fight in the previous round.

questions: What happens if an MMA fighter withdraws?
Are bets void if a replacement fighter is used?
What happens when there is a fighter substitution?
Can a fight continue if one fighter is replaced?
How are bets settled after a fighter withdrawal?
content: If either scheduled fighter withdraws from the bout or is replaced by another fighter before the contest takes place, all bets on that fight are declared void.

Are bets void if the fight ends as No Contest?
How are bets settled when there is no official winner?
What is the betting outcome for a No Contest fight?
content: If an MMA fight is officially declared a 'No Contest', all bets placed on that fight are void.

What does Over 2.5 rounds mean?
How are half rounds calculated?
What happens if the fight ends exactly at 2 minutes 30 seconds?
How is Over/Under betting settled in MMA?
When is a fight considered Over 2.5 rounds?
content: Total Rounds (Over/Under) betting predicts the round in which the fight result will be determined. For settlement purposes, a half round is measured at 2 minutes and 30 seconds of the relevant round. For example, Over/Under 2.5 rounds uses 2 minutes and 30 seconds of Round 3 as the reference point. If the fight ends exactly at that time, the result is settled as Over.

questions: How is the Winning Method market settled?
What counts as a knockout in MMA betting?
Does a doctor stoppage count as a knockout?
Does a corner stoppage count as a knockout?
Does retirement due to injury count as a knockout?
Does a disqualification count as a knockout?
What counts as a submission?
Does a technical submission count as a submission?
Does a verbal submission count as a submission?
How are Winning Method bets settled?
content: Winning Method betting predicts how the fight will be won and is settled according to the official result. A disqualification is treated as a Knockout/Technical Knockout. For settlement purposes, a Knockout includes referee stoppages due to strikes while standing or on the ground, doctor stoppages, corner or team stoppages, fighter retirement due to injury, and victories by disqualification. A Submission includes tap-outs, technical submissions, and verbal submissions, including verbal submissions caused by strikes.

Does disqualification count for Winner and Exact Round?
What happens if a fighter fails to answer the bell?
How are technical decisions settled?
What happens to round bets after a technical decision?
Can a decision victory win this market?
content: Winner and Exact Round betting predicts both the winning fighter and the exact round in which the fight is won by knockout (KO), technical knockout (TKO), submission, or disqualification, or alternatively by decision. If a fighter fails to answer the bell for the next round, the opponent is considered to have won in the previous round. If the fight ends by technical decision before completion, it is settled as a decision victory and all Winner & Exact Round round-specific bets lose.

questions: What does 'Will the Fight Go the Distance?' mean?
How is Go the Distance betting settled?
Does a technical decision count as going the distance?
What happens if the fight ends before the scheduled rounds?
How are Go the Distance bets settled in MMA?
content: The 'Will the Fight Go the Distance?' market predicts whether the fight will last for all scheduled rounds. If the fight ends before the scheduled distance, it is settled as not going the distance. For settlement purposes, a technical decision is also considered not to have gone the distance.

questions: When is a golfer considered to have participated in a tournament?
What happens if a golfer withdraws after teeing off?
How are bets settled if bad weather shortens a tournament?
What happens if a golf tournament is abandoned?
What happens if a golf round is abandoned?
Which official results are used for settlement?
Do later disqualifications affect settled bets?
What happens if play is delayed because of rain?
How are 2 Ball and 3 Ball bets settled if there is a non-runner?
When do golf bets stand after a player starts?
content: A golfer is considered to have participated once they tee off. If a player withdraws, retires, or is disqualified after teeing off, bets remain valid. If a tournament is shortened due to weather or similar reasons, bets are settled using the official tournament result regardless of the number of rounds completed. If the tournament is abandoned, bets placed after the last completed round are void. If an individual round is abandoned, all undecided markets are void. Official tour results at the time of trophy presentation are used for settlement, and later disqualifications are ignored. Delays caused by rain, darkness, or similar reasons do not void bets; unsettled markets remain open until play resumes. If there are non-runners, all 2 Ball and 3 Ball betting markets are void.

questions: How does 2 Ball betting work?
How does 3 Ball betting work?
What happens if both golfers retire in a 2 Ball market?
What happens if both golfers finish with the same score?
When is a golfer considered a runner?
Do dead heat rules apply in 3 Ball betting?
content: The 2 Ball market predicts which golfer records the lowest score in the specified round. If both golfers retire at the same hole or finish with the same score, the market is void. A golfer is considered a runner once they tee off. The 3 Ball market also predicts the golfer with the lowest score in the round, and dead heat rules apply.

questions: How is the Outright Winner market settled?
Do playoffs count for golf winner bets?
What happens if a tournament is shortened?
How is the Winner market settled?
What are the golf majors?
What does 'To Win a Major' mean?
When do Winner bets become active?
content: Outright Winner and Winner markets are settled using the official tournament winner, including playoff or extra-hole results. If a tournament is shortened because of weather or similar circumstances, outright bets placed before the final completed round are settled using the officially awarded winner. Winner bets remain valid once the listed golfer has teed off. The 'To Win a Major' market applies only to the US Masters, US Open, USPGA Championship, and British Open.

questions: How does Group Betting work?
How is Winner of Group settled?
What happens if only one golfer starts in a group?
How is Finishing Position betting settled?
How are ties handled in finishing positions?
Do dead heat rules apply to Top 10 betting?
How are Top 5 and Top 20 markets settled?
content: Group Betting and Winner of Group markets are settled using the golfer with the best finishing position or lowest tournament score within the specified group. If only one golfer starts in a group, the market is void. Finishing Position markets use the official finishing position, and tied positions count as the finishing position achieved. Dead heat rules apply to Group Betting, Winner of Group, and Top 4, Top 5, Top 6, Top 10, and Top 20 Finish markets unless a playoff determines the winner.

questions: How is End of Round Leader settled?
How is First Round Leader settled?
Do dead heat rules apply to Round Leader betting?
What happens if a golfer withdraws before the round?
What if a golfer never hits a shot?
content: End of Round Leader and similar markets are settled using the tournament scores at the completion of the specified round. Dead heat rules apply when two or more golfers share the lead. If a golfer does not hit a single shot in the tournament or withdraws before playing a shot in the relevant round, that golfer is void for End of Round Leader markets.

questions: What happens if a golfer retires in Competitor markets?
How are Total markets settled if a golfer withdraws?
What happens to Hole betting markets after a retirement?
When are Hole A to B markets void?
How are golfer withdrawals handled in player-specific markets?
content: If a listed golfer retires or withdraws, all undecided Competitor, Total, Hole, and Hole A to B betting markets involving that golfer are declared void.

questions: What happens if a motorcycle race is postponed?
What happens if a motorcycle racing event is abandoned?
Do bets remain valid after a postponed race?
How long does the postponed event have to be completed?
Are bets void if the race is delayed?
What is the 72-hour rule for motorcycle racing?
How are postponed Motorcycle Racing events settled?
When do motorcycle racing bets become void?
content: If a Motorcycle Racing event is postponed or abandoned, all bets remain valid provided that the event is completed within 72 hours of its original scheduled time. If the event is not completed within this 72-hour period, the bets will no longer remain valid and will be settled according to the applicable betting rules.

What happens if an athletics event is abandoned?
Do bets remain valid after a postponed athletics event?
How long does a postponed athletics event have to be completed?
What is the 72-hour rule in athletics betting?
Are athletics bets void if the event is delayed?

When do athletics bets become void?
content: If an Athletics event is postponed or abandoned, all bets remain valid provided that the event is completed within 72 hours of its original scheduled time. questions: What happens if a winter sports event is postponed?
What happens if a winter sports event is abandoned?

How long does a postponed winter sports event have to be completed?
What is the 72-hour rule for winter sports betting?
Are winter sports bets void if the event is delayed?
How are postponed winter sports events settled?
When do winter sports bets become void?

questions: How are Formula 1 bets settled?
Which result is used for Formula 1 settlement?
What happens if an F1 race is shortened?
What happens if a Formula 1 race is postponed?
What happens if a driver starts from the pit lane?
How are dead heats handled in Formula 1 betting?
How are retired drivers ranked?
What if multiple drivers retire?
content: Unless otherwise stated, Formula 1 markets are settled using the official result available at the time of the podium presentation. Races shortened due to weather or other circumstances are settled normally if the governing body declares the race official and full championship points are awarded. If a race is postponed to another day, all markets are void. Dead heat rules apply whenever there are more winners than expected for a market. Drivers starting from the pit lane are ranked behind the starting grid for settlement purposes. If dedicated driver selections retire on different laps, the number of completed laps determines the result.

questions: How are Formula 1 team markets settled?
How is Winner Team settled?
How is Top Team betting settled?
How does Team Head-to-Head work?
How is First Team to Retire settled?
How is First Team Pit Stop settled?
How are Team Overtakings calculated?
content: Winner (Team), Top X (Team), and Team Head-to-Head markets are settled using the team's highest-finishing car. First Team to Retire is settled according to the team whose car retires first, while First Pit Stop is settled using the first team whose car enters the pit lane. Team Overtakings are calculated using the combined overtaking total of both cars belonging to the same team.

questions: How is Fastest Lap betting settled?
Who wins the Fastest Lap market?
How are lap times measured?
Can I bet on the fastest lap?
content: Fastest Lap markets are settled in favor of the driver recording the fastest lap during the specified lap, group of laps, or the entire race. Official lap times measured in milliseconds are used for settlement.

questions: How are Formula 1 Head-to-Head markets settled?
What happens if both drivers retire?
What happens if a driver retires during the formation lap?
When are Head-to-Head bets void?
content: Head-to-Head and Winner of Group markets are void if every selected driver retires during the same lap. Markets are also void if any participating driver retires during or before the formation lap.

questions: How are overtaking bets settled?
What counts as an overtaking?
Do first lap overtakes count?
Do pit lane overtakes count?
Does lapping count as an overtake?
Does unlapping count as an overtake?
content: An overtaking counts only if the position is maintained until the end of the lap. Overtakes made during the opening lap, during pit entry or exit, or on the lap in which a driver retires are ignored. Lapping and unlapping are not considered overtaking for settlement purposes.

questions: When is a Formula 1 driver considered retired?
How are retirement markets settled?
What happens if two drivers retire on the same lap?
How is a pit lane retirement treated?
content: A driver is considered retired if the car does not cross the finish line when the session officially ends, unless the driver is disqualified. If multiple drivers retire on the same lap where the first retirement occurs, dead heat rules apply. When a car retires in the pit lane or pit area, the last lap started is used for settlement.

questions: How are Pit Stop markets settled?
Who wins the First Pit Stop market?
Does a retirement in the pit lane count as a pit stop?
content: Pit Stop markets are settled using the first car that enters the pit lane. A car that enters the pit lane and immediately retires is still considered to have made a valid pit stop for settlement purposes.

questions: Who is considered a finisher in Formula 1 betting?
How is the Total Finishers market settled?
What qualifies as finishing a Formula 1 race?
content: For Total Finishers markets, a driver is considered a finisher only if the car crosses the finish line when the race session is officially declared complete.

questions: How are chess bets settled?
What happens if a chess game is abandoned?
When are chess bets void?
How are chess moves counted?
Which game record is used for settlement?
What happens if a game is forfeited?
content: Unless otherwise stated, all bets relate to a single chess game. If a game is abandoned, forfeited, or not completed, all undecided markets are void unless the outcome has already been determined. Moves are counted when White makes a move, and all settlements are based on the official game protocol.

questions: Can I bet on the first chess move?
Can I bet on e4 or d4?
How is First Piece to Move settled?
What is the First Captured Piece market?
Can I bet on the opening move?
content: Opening markets include predicting the first move played (such as e4 or d4), the first piece type moved (Pawn or Knight), and the first captured piece (Pawn, Knight, Bishop, Rook, or Queen). These markets are settled according to the official game record.

questions: Can I bet on checkmate?
Can I bet on castling?
Can I bet on pawn promotion?
What is the En Passant market?
Can I bet on stalemate?
How is Total Castlings settled?
content: Special event markets include whether the game ends in checkmate, whether a stalemate occurs, whether an en passant capture happens, whether any pawn is promoted, and the total number of castlings performed by both players. Kingside and queenside castling are both counted.

questions: Can I bet on total moves?
How is Number of Checks settled?
What is Final Number of Pieces?
Who has more pieces at the end?
Can I bet on remaining pieces?
content: Game statistic markets include the total number of moves, total number of checks, final number of pieces remaining on the board, and which player finishes with more remaining pieces. Remaining pieces include pawns.

questions: Can I bet on checkmate before move 30?
Can I bet that the game ends before move 40?
Who gives the first check?
How are move-based markets settled?
content: Timing markets include predicting whether checkmate occurs before a specified move, whether the game finishes before a specified move number, and which player gives the first check. Move numbers are counted when White makes a move.

questions: Who will finish higher in the tournament?
How are tournament standings settled?
What happens if players tie?
What happens if a player never starts the tournament?
content: Tournament position markets are settled using the official tournament leaderboard. Official tie-break rules published by the organizer are used whenever applicable. If no official tie-break is applied or a player never starts the tournament, related bets are void.

questions: Who wins more games with White?
Who wins more games with Black?
What is Player Total Wins?
How is Player Total Points calculated?
Can I bet that a player starts 3-0?
How is Total Combined Wins settled?
content: Tournament performance markets include total wins, wins with White pieces, wins with Black pieces, combined wins by both players, player total points, and whether a player starts the tournament with three consecutive victories. Wins, draws, losses, forfeits, and withdrawals are settled according to the official tournament results and the specific market rules.

questions: How are esports bets settled?
Which results are used to settle esports bets?
What happens if the match start time is incorrect?
Will bets stand if the match date is wrong?
What happens if a player or team name is misspelled?
What happens if a team changes its name?
Do stand-in players affect bet settlement?
Can bets still stand when substitute players are used?
Which stream is used as the official result?
content: All esports markets are settled using the official in-game results or the official event broadcast. Incorrect match dates or times do not affect valid bets. Misspelled player, team, or tournament names do not invalidate bets unless they clearly identify another entity. Team name changes due to organizational changes do not affect settlement. If tournament organizers allow stand-in players and an official result is declared, all bets remain valid.

content: If a runner is scratched from a race, the customer's stake will be refunded.

questions: What happens if a race is abandoned?
What if a race is postponed?
What if a race is transferred to another venue?
When do postponed race bets remain valid?
What happens if scratchings are reinstated?
How are combo bets affected by postponed races?
Do postponed races within 48 hours keep my bet active?
content: If a race is abandoned, transferred to another venue or track, or postponed to another date, all affected single bets are void and Combo Bets are recalculated excluding that event. If the race is postponed and rescheduled at the same venue within 48 hours of the original start time, all bets remain valid. If scratchings are reinstated following a postponed race at the same venue, all bets on that race become void.

questions: What are deduction rules?
When are deductions applied?
How are deductions calculated?
Do scratched runners affect winnings?
What happens when multiple runners are scratched?
How are deduction percentages calculated?
Are deductions applied to winnings or stake?
content: Bets may be subject to deductions after they have been placed. Deductions are applied to the expected winnings (face value) of winning bets when runners are scratched after the final field has been declared. Deduction amounts are calculated as percentages of the winnings. If multiple runners are scratched, the combined deduction is calculated by adding together the deduction percentages for each scratched runner according to the official Deductions Table.

questions: Where can I find the deductions table?
How much deduction applies to my odds?
What deduction percentage applies to Win betting?
What deduction percentage applies to Place betting?
How are Top 2 deductions calculated?
Which deduction percentage applies for scratched runners?
What is the official deductions table?
content: The official Deductions Table defines the deduction percentage applied to Win, Top 2 and Place markets based on the odds of each scratched runner. Deduction percentages decrease as the odds increase. For odds of 20.00 or higher, no deductions are applied. The applicable deduction percentage is determined using the published Deductions Table.

questions: What happens if incorrect odds are published?
Can the sportsbook void bets placed on incorrect odds?

What happens if the sportsbook posts incorrect betting information?
Are bets on erroneous odds valid?
Does the sportsbook have the right to void bets caused by system or pricing errors?
content: If the sportsbook publishes, posts, or quotes incorrect betting information for any Greyhound, Horse or Harness Racing event, including incorrect odds, the sportsbook reserves the right to void any affected bets regardless of the cause or source of the error.

content: If a single bet is inadvertently accepted after the official start time of a Greyhound, Horse or Harness Racing event, the bet will be declared void and the customer's stake will be refunded.

content: If a bet is accepted after the official start time of a race as part of a Combo Bet, only that affected event will be treated as void. The remaining selections in the Combo Bet will continue to stand and be settled according to the applicable betting rules.

questions: What happens if a horse is withdrawn late?
What happens if a greyhound is withdrawn by the stewards?
How are late withdrawals handled?
Do deductions apply after a late withdrawal?
How are bets settled when a runner is withdrawn by the stewards?
Are remaining runners subject to deductions after a late scratching?
What rules apply to steward-ordered withdrawals?
content: If a horse or greyhound is withdrawn late by order of the stewards, bets will be settled according to the stewards' official decision regarding the runner's status. Applicable deductions will be applied to the remaining runners in accordance with the official Deductions Table.

questions: Which race result is used for settlement?
What happens if a horse is disqualified after race day?
What if the official placings change later?
Do later disqualifications affect settled bets?
How are steward decisions used for bet settlement?
Which official result determines winnings?
Are bets recalculated after race-day amendments?
content: All bets are settled according to the official decision of the stewards on race day. If a horse or greyhound is later disqualified or the placings are amended after race day, the original official result declared by the stewards on the day of the race remains the final result for bet settlement purposes.
